en.intro: Krishna has just named the qualities of a fearless soul. Now he lists the inner habits that make that courage possible. Listen for one quality that protects others from harm.
en.notice: Krishna lists ten virtues, and among them is apaisunam, the absence of slander. This quality protects others not through action but through the restraint of speech.
en.next: Krishna continues with the qualities of splendor, forgiveness, and steadiness that mark a divine nature.
en.meaning: Nonviolence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, inner calm, absence of slander, compassion for all beings, freedom from greed, gentleness, modesty, and absence of restlessness.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी एक निडर आत्मा के गुणों का नाम लिया है। अब वे उन आंतरिक आदतों को बताते हैं जिनसे वह साहस संभव होता है।
hi.meaning: अहिंसा, सत्यभाषण, क्रोध न करना, त्याग, अन्तःकरण में रागद्वेष जनित हलचल न होना, चुगली न करना, प्राणियों पर दया करना, सांसारिक विषयों में न ललचाना, अन्तःकरण की कोमलता, अकर्तव्य करने में लज्जा और चपलता का अभाव।
hi.next: कृष्ण आगे उन गुणों के बारे में बताते हैं जिनमें तेज, क्षमा, स्थिरता और पवित्रता शामिल हैं जो एक दिव्य स्वभाव की पहचान हैं।

issues: wrong_fact: "सुनिए, एक ऐसा गुण जो दूसरों को नुकसान से बचाता है।" (This phrase in the Hindi intro claims that one specific quality (implied to be nonviolence/ahimsa) protects others from harm. However, the verse lists multiple qualities (nonviolence, truth, freedom from anger, etc.) that collectively protect others, and it does not single out one. Furthermore, the next verse (verse 3) is about splendor and forgiveness, not nonviolence protecting others from harm.)

unsupported: "गुणों की इस लंबी सूची में यह अकेला गुण है जो केवल चुप रहकर दूसरों को नुकसान से बचाता है।" (This claim in the Hindi notice that 'apaisunam' (absence of slander) is the only quality that protects others by staying silent is an unsupported interpretation. The verse simply lists 'apaisunam' alongside other virtues (like nonviolence) as a standard for a divine life, without stating that it is the only silent protector or that it uniquely protects others.)

meaning_changed: "संसार की कामना का त्याग" (The source Hindi translation gives 'संसारकी कामनाका त्याग' (renunciation of worldly desires) for the Sanskrit word 'त्यागः' (renunciation). The app's Hindi text changes this to 'संसार की कामना का त्याग' (renunciation of the desire for the world). This softens the meaning by limiting 'tyāga' specifically to the renunciation of worldly desires, whereas 'tyāga' in this context is a broad virtue of renunciation, not necessarily restricted to 'sāṃsārika kāmanā'.)

meaning_changed: "अन्तःकरण में रागद्वेष से उत्पन्न होने वाली हलचल का न होना" (The source Hindi translation gives 'अन्तःकरणमें रागद्वेषजनित हलचलका न होना' (absence of agitation born of attachment and aversion in the inner being) for the Sanskrit word 'शान्तिः' (calm). The app's Hindi text changes this to 'अन्तःकरण में रागद्वेष से उत्पन्न होने वाली हलचल का न होना' (absence of agitation arising from attachment and aversion in the inner being). This changes the meaning of 'śānti' from inner calm/peace to the absence of agitation caused by attachment and aversion, which is a different concept (more aligned with 'apaisunam' or 'ātmaviṣaya' concepts) rather than the standalone virtue of calmness.)
